record.paper_title: Solutions to Some Open Problems from Slaney
record.original_question: In the positive sentential logic TW+[Ax L, AxTO]—whose pure implicational fragment TW→ has axioms AxB, AxI, AxB0, Ax L, and AxTO together with the rule Det, and whose full positive extension additionally includes the conjunction and disjunction axioms/rules Ax∧E1, Ax∧E2, Ax∧I, Ax∨I1, Ax∨I2, Ax∨E, and Adj—is the distributivity schema (Dist), namely (A ∧ (B ∨ C)) → ((A ∧ B) ∨ (A ∧ C)), derivable?

evidence.quote: Specifically, Slaney’s open questions involve the following three (background) positive logics. 1. TW+[Ax L, AxTO], the pure implicational fragment of which (TW→) is given by the axioms AxB, AxI, AxB0, Ax L, and AxTO, and the rule Det. The full logic TW+[Ax L, AxTO] is then obtained by adding all of the axioms and rules for conjunction and disjunction to this implicational base.
1. Is (Dist) provable in TW+[Ax L, AxTO]?
Our first theorem therefore implies affirmative answers to both (1) and (2). Theorem 1. (IO) is provable in TW+[Ax L, AxTO].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the positive sentential logic L defined as follows. The language has propositional variables and the connectives →, ∧, ∨. The pure implicational fragment L→ is the Hilbert-style system with the following axiom schemas and rule:

• (AxB)  (B → C) → ((A → B) → (A → C))
• (AxI)  A → A
• (AxB0) (A → B) → ((C → A) → (C → B))
• (Ax L) ((A → B) ∧ (B → C)) → (A → C)    (here, when stated for the implicational fragment, taken in its appropriate purely implicational form; the conjunction is added with its axioms below)
• (AxTO) A → ((A → B) → B)
• (Det)  from A and A → B infer B (modus ponens).

The full positive logic L = TW+[Ax L, AxTO] is obtained by adding to this implicational base the standard axioms and rule for conjunction and disjunction:

• (Ax∧E1) (A ∧ B) → A
• (Ax∧E2) (A ∧ B) → B
• (Ax∧I) ((A → B) ∧ (A → C)) → (A → (B ∧ C))
• (Ax∨I1) A → (A ∨ B)
• (Ax∨I2) B → (A ∨ B)
• (Ax∨E) ((A → C) ∧ (B → C)) → ((A ∨ B) → C)
• (Adj) from A and B infer A ∧ B.

Question: Is the distributivity schema
    (Dist)  (A ∧ (B ∨ C)) → ((A ∧ B) ∨ (A ∧ C))
derivable in L?
artifact.status_search_result: The question has been answered in the affirmative: distributivity (Dist) is provable in TW+[Ax L, AxTO]. This follows from a theorem establishing the provability of a related schema (IO) in the same system, which yields (Dist) as a consequence.
